speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are an infant presenting with recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing, particularly during specific activities. To help me understand your condition, please tell me exactly what those specific activities are that seem to trigger these breathing difficulties.

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the worsening of symptoms with neck flexion and vomiting is a very specific finding. Given the infant's age and the combination of stridor, wheezing during crying, and post-feed vomiting, do you have any family history of gastrointestinal issues or known structural anomalies? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Neck_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

The clinical presentation of inspiratory stridor exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, accompanied by post-feeding vomiting, is classic for this diagnosis. The relief with neck extension further supports a dynamic airway collapse of the supraglottic structures rather than a fixed obstruction.
